title: Submission metadata can link the student to a specific assignment submission
description: The portal receives student id, course, timestamp, and the submitted work file in a single flow. These attributes together directly link the submission event and content to an identifiable student, enabling correlation of actions and records across assignments and courses.
assumptions: The web app or downstream systems store or can observe these fields together.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best estimate for linkability via identifying/observable metadata; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Student identity is disclosed to parties that do not need it for handling the upload
description: If the flow or its immediate processing exposes student id together with course and assignment content to components, operators, logs, or integrations beyond those necessary for submission handling, the student's identity is unnecessarily revealed.
assumptions: Some portal components, support staff, logs, or integrated services may access raw submission requests.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for identifiability/identity disclosure from direct identifiers in the flow.

title: Assignment file and submission details may be disclosed in transit or through logging
description: The uploaded work file, student id, course, and submission timestamp are privacy-sensitive educational records. If transport protection is weak, session handling is flawed, or request bodies are logged, unauthorized parties could access this data.
assumptions: Threat includes network interception, browser/proxy leakage, or server-side request logging.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate fit for information disclosure of communicated/stored personal data.

title: Student may be unable to prove what was submitted and when
description: If the portal does not provide reliable evidence such as signed receipts, immutable timestamps, or verifiable submission records, the student could later be unable to demonstrate that a particular file was submitted at a specific time.
assumptions: The system may rely only on mutable server records or lacks user-verifiable receipts.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for repudiation due to insufficient evidence of an action.

title: Students may be unaware of how submissions and metadata are processed
description: At login and submission, the student may not be adequately informed about collection, retention, access, plagiarism scanning, or sharing of the work file and associated metadata. This undermines predictability and user awareness about processing.
assumptions: The portal may not present clear just-in-time notice for submission processing.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node id for lack of awareness/transparency; exact LINDDUN Pro mapping may differ.

title: Collection or further use of submission data may exceed privacy obligations
description: The flow collects identifiable educational content and metadata. If the portal lacks a valid basis, collects more data than necessary, retains submissions too long, or reuses them for analytics or model training without appropriate authorization, processing may be non-compliant.
assumptions: Applicable educational/privacy obligations require purpose limitation, minimization, retention limits, and appropriate legal basis/notice.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node id for policy/legal non-compliance; exact tree node may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Submission and grading requests may enable linking of a student across courses and assignments
description: The routed request contains student id, course, file reference, and requesting role. If identifiers are reused and visible across processing contexts, the assignment service can correlate multiple submissions, grading events, and course participation for the same student, enabling cross-context linkage beyond what is necessary for a single transaction.
assumptions: Student id is persistent across courses or terms and is exposed to the receiving process in each request.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for linkability on a process-to-process flow may differ.

title: Student identity and course enrollment may be inferred from routed request metadata
description: Because the flow includes student id and course, the receiving service learns or can infer that a specific student is enrolled in or interacting with a particular course and assignment. Even if file content is not included, the combination of metadata reveals identity-associated academic activity.
assumptions: Assignment & Grading Service does not strictly need all attributes for every request or multiple internal actors can observe the request.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for identifiability/disclosure from data attributes on the flow.

title: Academic activity details may be disclosed to unauthorized internal recipients or logs
description: Submission and grading requests may be logged, monitored, or exposed within the receiving service, disclosing student id, course membership, file references, and role information to parties not authorized to access that academic record information.
assumptions: The receiving service or its infrastructure generates application, audit, or transport logs containing request fields.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node id; exact subtree may vary depending on whether disclosure is to an internal actor, storage, or transit observer.

title: A requester may later deny having initiated a submission or grading action
description: If the portal forwards requests without strong binding between the authenticated actor, the exact action, and a verifiable audit record, a student, instructor, or staff member could repudiate having submitted work or requested a grading-related action.
assumptions: Requests may not be cryptographically signed or immutably logged with actor identity and timestamp.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-repudiation gap on an inter-process request flow.

title: Users may be unaware that assignment metadata is propagated to a separate grading service
description: Students or staff using the portal may not understand that their student id, course, file reference, and role are sent onward to another backend service for processing, limiting transparency about recipients and processing purposes.
assumptions: The portal interface or privacy notice does not clearly disclose backend sharing and purpose.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for unawareness/transparency deficiency; exact node label may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Routing full student and course identifiers may exceed data minimization or purpose limitation requirements
description: The portal may send more personal data than necessary for the grading service to perform a given operation. For example, persistent student identifiers or role details may be unnecessary when a scoped pseudonymous token or per-request authorization context would suffice, creating non-compliance risk with privacy obligations.
assumptions: Some requests could be fulfilled using reduced or pseudonymized attributes.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node id; exact LINDDUN Pro compliance subtree may differ.

title: Stored assignment records are linkable across courses and submissions via persistent student identifier
description: The grading service stores assignment files together with a student id, course, and submission time. A persistent student identifier in the store can enable linking multiple submissions by the same student across assignments and potentially across courses, revealing behavior patterns and academic history.
assumptions: Assignment Store retains records over time and uses a stable student identifier accessible to internal actors or systems.
uncertainty_note: Node id is my best fit for linkability from stored identifiers; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree naming may vary.

title: Student identity can be inferred from stored metadata and assignment content
description: The stored tuple of assignment file, student id, course, and submission time directly identifies the student, and even if direct identifiers were reduced, assignment content plus course and timing may still allow re-identification or identity inference.
assumptions: Stored data is accessible to parties beyond those strictly needing direct identification, or identifiers may later be pseudonymized while content remains.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for identifiability; exact Pro node label may differ.

title: Sensitive academic and behavioral information is disclosed through stored submissions and metadata
description: Assignment files may contain personal opinions, writing style, special-category information, or other sensitive content. Combined with course and submission time, the store can disclose academic performance patterns, working habits, and participation details if accessed inappropriately.
assumptions: Assignment contents and metadata are readable by administrators, other services, or attackers without sufficient minimization or access control.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort mapping to a generic information disclosure node.

title: Students may be unable to deny or contest a stored submission record
description: By storing student id together with submission time and file, the system creates evidence that a specific student submitted a specific assignment at a specific time. If logging, consent, or submission confirmation mechanisms are unclear, the student may not be able to meaningfully repudiate or challenge erroneous or fraudulent records.
assumptions: Submission records are treated as authoritative and there may be account sharing, credential compromise, or processing errors.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for non-repudiation concerns around authoritative submission evidence.

title: Storage of full assignment files with identifiers may exceed necessity or retention needs
description: Persisting the complete assignment file alongside direct student id, course, and exact submission time may constitute storing more personal data than necessary for grading, especially after grading is complete or where less precise metadata would suffice.
assumptions: There is no defined minimization or retention policy limiting fields, precision of timestamps, or duration of storage.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for data minimization / excessive collection or retention.

title: Students may lack awareness of what submission metadata and content are retained
description: If the service does not clearly inform students that the assignment file, student id, course association, and exact submission time are stored in the Assignment Store, students may be unaware of the extent, purpose, or duration of processing.
assumptions: Privacy notices or just-in-time explanations are incomplete or absent.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for lack of transparency/unawareness.

title: Storage of identifiable assignment data may not comply with purpose limitation, minimization, or retention obligations
description: Storing identifiable submissions and detailed metadata can violate privacy requirements if the data is kept longer than necessary, reused beyond grading-related purposes, or lacks an appropriate legal basis and governance controls.
assumptions: Applicable education/privacy policies or regulations impose purpose limitation, retention, and minimization requirements.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for non-compliance; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may differ.

title: Teacher identity can be identified from authentication and request metadata
description: The login and queue-request flow necessarily carries account identifiers and related authentication metadata, allowing the web app to identify which teacher is accessing the system and tying the request to a specific staff member.
assumptions: The teacher authenticates with a unique account or SSO identity before requesting the submission-review queue.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate because exact LINDDUN Pro tree labels may vary by version.

title: Teacher requests may be linkable across sessions and courses
description: Repeated login events and queue requests can be linked to the same teacher account, enabling construction of patterns about teaching assignments, workload, review habits, and activity times across courses and sessions.
assumptions: The application logs authenticated requests, session identifiers, IP/device data, or course-selection events.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact subtree for linkability of repeated interactions may differ in a specific LINDDUN Pro catalog.

title: Request reveals the teacher's course affiliations and review activity
description: By requesting the queue of submissions for their courses, the teacher discloses which courses they are associated with and that they are currently engaged in reviewing submissions, exposing role, workload, and timing information beyond simple authentication.
assumptions: The portal or supporting infrastructure can observe the specific queue endpoint, parameters, or resulting course-scoped access.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact disclosure subtree may differ depending on whether emphasis is on content, metadata, or activity disclosure.

title: Teacher may be unable to plausibly deny having accessed a submission queue
description: If the portal records successful authentication and queue access events with timestamps and account identifiers, those logs can be used to prove that a specific teacher accessed the submission-review queue, reducing plausible deniability for that action.
assumptions: Access logs are retained and attributable to the teacher's account.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; non-repudiation tree node naming may vary across LINDDUN Pro versions.

title: Insufficient transparency about monitoring of teacher access behavior
description: The teacher may not be adequately informed that login attempts, queue requests, timestamps, IP/device data, and course-access patterns are monitored, logged, or used for analytics, making data processing around this flow insufficiently detectable to the teacher.
assumptions: The portal presents limited or unclear notice about operational logging, analytics, or administrative monitoring.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact detectability subtree label may vary.

title: Authentication and access logging may exceed stated purpose or legal basis
description: The portal may process more personal data than necessary during teacher login and queue retrieval—such as detailed behavioral analytics, persistent identifiers, or extended retention of access logs—without an appropriate purpose limitation, minimization rationale, or clear legal basis.
assumptions: The system collects or retains access metadata beyond what is strictly required for secure operation and authorization.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact non-compliance subtree depends on the applicable compliance objective in the LINDDUN Pro model.

title: Unauthorized teacher access to submissions outside assigned students/classes
description: If the portal does not properly enforce authorization before displaying submissions, a teacher may view student names, work content, and submission times for students or classes they are not permitted to access.
assumptions: Assumes access control is enforced by the portal and misconfiguration, privilege escalation, or missing checks are possible on this display flow.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for unauthorized access/disclosure on a process-to-user display flow; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree naming may vary.

title: Submissions can be linked to identified students across courses or contexts
description: Because the portal displays student names together with work content and timestamps, the teacher can readily correlate submissions belonging to the same student across assignments, courses, or time periods, enabling broader profiling than necessary for the immediate task.
assumptions: Assumes the portal exposes stable identifiers or names across multiple records and contexts.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-effort match for linkability created by exposing directly identifying attributes together with event data.

title: Student identity is directly disclosed with submitted work
description: Displaying student names alongside submission content reveals the identity of the submitter to the teacher. This may exceed what is necessary in workflows that could support blind or pseudonymous marking.
assumptions: Assumes some educational contexts require or benefit from reduced identity exposure during assessment.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit identifiability node; exact tree node numbering may differ.

title: Excessive disclosure of submission metadata
description: The portal reveals submission times in addition to names and work content. Exact timestamps may disclose behavioral patterns, working habits, lateness, location/time-zone inferences, or special circumstances that are not necessary for all teaching tasks.
assumptions: Assumes fine-grained timestamps are shown and not strictly required for every viewer or use case.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for detectability/disclosure via observable metadata; exact subtree may vary in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Teacher can deny having viewed particular student submissions
description: If the portal does not maintain reliable audit logs of access/display events, a teacher may later repudiate having accessed a given student's submission, complicating accountability and incident investigation.
assumptions: Assumes viewing events may need to be provable for accountability or complaint handling.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit repudiation node; exact numbering may differ depending on the tree variant.

title: Students may be unaware that detailed submission data is shown to teachers
description: If the system does not clearly inform students that their names, work content, and precise submission times are presented to teachers, students may misunderstand the extent and context of visibility of their personal data.
assumptions: Assumes transparency notices or in-context explanations may be absent or incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit unawareness node; exact LINDDUN Pro numbering may vary.

title: Displaying identifiable submissions may conflict with data minimization or purpose limitation
description: Showing full student names, full work content, and exact submission timestamps to every teacher recipient may violate privacy requirements if only a subset of that data is necessary for grading or feedback, or if blind marking policies apply.
assumptions: Assumes applicable policy, institutional rule, or legal basis may require minimization, role restriction, or pseudonymization.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node; exact numbering may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of grades and feedback in transit or at ingestion
description: The flow contains highly sensitive educational data: grade, written feedback, student id, and grader id. If the web app accepts or handles this submission over an insufficiently protected channel, or exposes it during request processing/logging, an attacker could learn a student's performance information and the teacher's assessment.
assumptions: Assumes the submission could be exposed via weak transport protection, intermediary logging, or insecure request handling.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure of data contents during communication/processing; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary by catalog wording.

title: Teacher actions are identifiable from grader id and submission metadata
description: Because the flow includes grader id together with grade and feedback, the teacher who authored a specific assessment can be directly identified. This may expose staff evaluation patterns or enable monitoring of individual teachers' grading behavior.
assumptions: Assumes grader id is a direct identifier or readily mapped to an individual teacher.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit for identifiability from direct identifiers in the message.

title: Grade submissions can be linked to other records about the same student or teacher
description: Student id and grader id in the same flow allow the submission to be linked with other portal records, course rosters, prior assignments, or staff activity logs. This can reveal broader performance histories and teacher behavior over time beyond the immediate purpose of recording one assignment result.
assumptions: Assumes identifiers are reused across assignments/courses or are correlatable with other system datasets.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability via shared identifiers; exact subtree label may differ.

title: Teacher may be unable to deny authorship of a submitted grade/feedback entry
description: If the portal stores the submission together with grader id, timestamps, session identifiers, or audit metadata, the record may serve as evidence that a particular teacher entered the grade and feedback. This creates a privacy risk where the teacher cannot plausibly deny having performed the action.
assumptions: Assumes the system keeps actionable audit trails or persistent attribution tied to the teacher.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-repudiation caused by attributable action logging; exact node may vary.

title: Collection of student and teacher identifiers with free-text feedback may exceed necessity
description: The flow collects student id, grader id, numeric/textual grade data, and unrestricted written feedback. Depending on the grading purpose, retaining direct identifiers and free-text comments at submission time may be more personal data than necessary, especially if pseudonymous grading or minimized metadata would suffice.
assumptions: Assumes some grading workflows could operate with reduced identifiers or constrained feedback collection.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for data minimization / necessity concerns; exact LINDDUN Pro node may differ.

title: Teachers or students may be unaware how grades and feedback submissions are used or retained
description: When a teacher submits grade and feedback data, the subsequent uses may include audit logging, analytics, visibility to students/guardians, moderation, or long-term retention. If those uses are not clearly communicated, the involved parties may be unaware of processing purposes, recipients, or retention periods.
assumptions: Assumes insufficient transparency notices or contextual information at submission time.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of awareness/transparency; exact subtree wording may vary.

title: Stored grade record reveals sensitive academic performance and evaluator information
description: The grading service writes student id, course, grade, feedback, grader id, and timestamp into the grade records database. If the datastore is queried or accessed beyond strictly authorized educational purposes, the record directly discloses a student's academic performance and feedback, and also exposes the grader's identity and grading activity.
assumptions: The grade records database stores raw records in identifiable form and may be accessible to administrators, support staff, analytics components, or other internal actors beyond the immediate grading function.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id chosen as a generic information-disclosure storage threat; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary.

title: Grade records are linkable across courses and time
description: Because each write includes student id together with course, grade, feedback, grader id, and timestamp, records in the database can be linked to build longitudinal profiles of a student's academic history and of a grader's grading behavior across courses or assessment events.
assumptions: The same student id and grader id are reused across multiple records and the database supports retrieval or analysis across courses or terms.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id chosen as a generic linkability threat for persistent identifiers in a datastore; exact subtree may differ.

title: Inference of student circumstances from detailed feedback and timestamps
description: Even if direct access to the full record is somewhat restricted, detailed written feedback and grading timestamps can reveal or enable inference about a student's weaknesses, accommodations, late submissions, appeals, or other special circumstances. Grader id and timing may also reveal workload or employment patterns of staff.
assumptions: Feedback may contain free text and timestamps may be precise enough to support secondary analysis.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate best fit for inference from stored attributes rather than direct disclosure.

title: Grader may be unable to plausibly deny authorship of a recorded grade submission
description: The write operation stores grader id and timestamp with the grade record, creating durable evidence that a specific grader entered or approved a grade at a specific time. While useful for accountability, this can create a privacy threat if records are later reused outside legitimate academic governance or exposed to parties who should not see staff activity traces.
assumptions: The recorded grader id is attributable to an individual and retained for long periods.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id chosen as a generic non-repudiation threat due to logging/attribution; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary.

title: Identifiability of student and grader from stored identifiers
description: The grade record explicitly includes student id and grader id, making both data subjects directly identifiable in the datastore. Anyone with access to the stored records can identify which student received which grade and which staff member performed the grading.
assumptions: Student id and grader id are directly mapped to real individuals within the organization.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id chosen as a generic identifiability threat for direct identifiers in storage.

title: Use of grade records beyond grading and academic administration may exceed expectations or legal basis
description: The database stores detailed identifiable grade records that could later be reused for analytics, staff performance monitoring, training, or student profiling without adequate transparency, purpose limitation, or consent/other appropriate legal basis. Such secondary use would create non-compliance risk.
assumptions: Policies or notices may not fully specify all downstream uses of grade, feedback, and grader-attribution data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id chosen as a generic policy/legal non-compliance threat; exact subtree may differ.

title: Request metadata can be linked to the student's identity and behaviour
description: When the student requests grades and feedback, the portal can associate the request with the student's authenticated account, timestamps, IP address, device/browser characteristics, and course context. Over time this can link multiple accesses into a behavioural profile of when the student checks results and feedback.
assumptions: The portal or supporting infrastructure logs authenticated requests and related metadata.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for linkability of request metadata to the same data subject; exact LINDDUN Pro node wording may differ.

title: Portal can identify the student from the grades request
description: To return the student's own grades, the portal identifies the requester, typically via login session, student number, or SSO attributes. This makes the request directly attributable to a specific student.
assumptions: The portal requires authentication or otherwise receives identifying account attributes.
uncertainty_note: Identification is inherent to serving 'own grades'; this is only a privacy threat if identification exceeds what is necessary or is exposed more broadly than intended. Node id is best-effort.

title: Sensitive academic information may be disclosed to unauthorized parties
description: The request and resulting handling of grades/feedback may expose sensitive academic records if the portal, logs, intermediaries, browser caches, or session handling allow access by unauthorized users or staff. Even the fact that a particular student requested grades at a given time may be sensitive.
assumptions: Grades and feedback are personal data and access-control, transport, or storage protections may be imperfect.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for disclosure of content or related metadata; exact subtree placement may vary in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Student may be unaware of logging and secondary use of grades-access data
description: The portal may collect request metadata such as timestamps, device details, course selections, and navigation context without making the student sufficiently aware of what is observed, retained, or shared for analytics, support, or monitoring.
assumptions: The system performs operational logging or analytics beyond the minimum strictly necessary to serve the request.
uncertainty_note: This is a detectability/unawareness boundary case; I classify it as unawareness because the main issue is lack of transparency to the student.

title: Insufficient transparency about processing of grades request data
description: The student may not be informed clearly about what personal data is processed when requesting grades and feedback, for what purposes, how long it is retained, and who can access it. This limits informed expectations and user agency.
assumptions: Privacy notices or in-context explanations are incomplete, generic, or absent.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node for lack of awareness/transparency; exact node naming in LINDDUN Pro may differ.

title: Processing of grades-access data may not comply with privacy obligations
description: The portal's handling of the student's request data and educational records may violate obligations such as data minimization, purpose limitation, retention limits, lawful basis, student access rights, or confidentiality requirements for education records.
assumptions: Applicable legal/policy obligations exist for student records and request logs.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance depends on jurisdiction and implementation details; node id is best-effort.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of grades and feedback to someone other than the student
description: If the portal response is delivered to the wrong recipient or exposed through weak session handling, missing access control, shared-device leakage, or interception, the student's grades and teacher feedback could be disclosed to an unauthorized person.
assumptions: The web app transmits individualized academic records over a network and relies on authentication/session state to identify the student.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id. I am confident this is an Information Disclosure threat, but the exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary by catalog version.

title: Linkability of academic records to the same student across sessions or contexts
description: Grades and feedback shown through the portal may include persistent identifiers, stable URLs, or correlatable metadata that allow observers or other systems to link multiple accesses and records to the same student over time.
assumptions: The portal may expose stable account identifiers or record references in responses, logs, or browser artifacts.
uncertainty_note: The exact node id is approximate; this is a generic linkability risk on a personalized results flow.

title: Overly identifying presentation of student information with grades
description: The portal may present the student's full identity together with grades and teacher feedback in a way that unnecessarily reveals identity in contexts such as shared screens, screenshots, browser previews, notifications, or logs.
assumptions: The app may display name, student number, class, or other direct identifiers alongside academic results.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact subtree for identifiability/presentation may differ across LINDDUN Pro versions.

title: Student cannot later deny having received or viewed the grades/feedback
description: If the portal records detailed access events or acknowledgements tied to the student, those records can be used to prove that the student viewed specific grades or teacher feedback, reducing plausible deniability about receipt or access.
assumptions: The system may keep access logs, read receipts, timestamps, IPs, or acknowledgement events linked to the student account.
uncertainty_note: This is a plausible non-repudiation/privacy concern, but applicability depends on whether access logging or acknowledgements are implemented.

title: Insufficient transparency or control over disclosure of grades and feedback
description: The student may not be clearly informed how long grades/feedback remain visible, whether access is logged, whether data is cached on devices, or whether onward sharing/export is possible, limiting informed control over their academic data.
assumptions: The portal may lack clear privacy notices or controls around retention, caching, export, and access logging for displayed records.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; this is framed as non-compliance/insufficient information and control, but exact mapping may vary.

title: Unwanted disclosure through browser, device, or caching artifacts
description: Even when only the student is meant to see the page, grades and feedback may persist in browser cache, auto-complete, notifications, screen previews, or shared-device history, enabling later disclosure to others.
assumptions: The student may access the portal from shared or unmanaged devices, and the application may not set cache-control or privacy-preserving display behaviors appropriately.
uncertainty_note: I am confident in the threat category, but the exact Dd node id is approximate.

title: Portal can identify which parent is requesting which child's grades
description: The login and request flow reveals the identity of the parent account and its linkage to a specific child account to the web app. If the portal collects or exposes more identifying attributes than necessary, staff, logs, or integrated components may learn the parent-child relationship and associated educational records.
assumptions: The web app authenticates the parent and knows the linked child account in order to serve grades.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree label for identify/data association may differ.

title: Request is linkable across sessions and over time
description: Repeated grade requests from the same parent account can be linked together by account identifier, session cookies, IP address, or device fingerprints. This can enable profiling of parental behavior, interest in specific courses or grading periods, and long-term tracking of access patterns.
assumptions: The portal uses persistent identifiers or logs request metadata.
uncertainty_note: Exact LINDDUN Pro linkability node id may be more specific than L.1.

title: Sensitive educational data may be disclosed to an unauthorized or wrong parent
description: If parent-child account linking is incorrect, stale, or insufficiently verified, the portal may return a child's grades to a parent who is not authorized to see them. Disclosure can also occur through weak authentication, session mix-up, broken access control, or insecure transmission.
assumptions: Parent access is based on an account linkage that may be misconfigured or attacked.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node chosen broadly for disclosure; exact disclosure subtree for unauthorized access or data transfer may differ.

title: Inference of child status from login and request metadata
description: Even if full grades are not shown, metadata such as the existence of a linked child account, timing and frequency of grade checks, class identifiers, or response sizes can disclose sensitive information about the child's enrollment, academic events, or performance trends.
assumptions: The system logs or exposes metadata to operators, third parties, or observers.
uncertainty_note: Could also map to detectability/information disclosure depending on the exact LINDDUN Pro tree interpretation.

title: Parent may later repudiate having requested grades
description: Without strong, integrity-protected audit trails, the parent could deny having logged in or requested access to the child's grades. This can hinder investigation of privacy incidents or disputes about who viewed educational records.
assumptions: Audit logging may be weak, mutable, or not tied strongly to the authenticated session.
uncertainty_note: Exact non-repudiation node id may differ in LINDDUN Pro nomenclature.

title: Parent may be unaware of what data and relationships are exposed during the request
description: The portal may not clearly inform the parent about what personal data is processed when requesting grades, such as the child-account linkage, logging of access events, sharing with analytics providers, or retention of access history. This reduces transparency and informed user expectations.
assumptions: Privacy notices or contextual explanations are incomplete or absent in the grade-request flow.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for unawareness/transparency from memory.

title: Processing may exceed consent or legal authorization for parent access
description: The portal may process or disclose a child's grades to a logged-in parent without verifying that the parent is legally entitled to access that student's records, or may continue access after custody/consent status changes. This creates risk of non-compliance with education privacy obligations and purpose limitations.
assumptions: Authorization depends on legal/administrative relationship that can change over time.
uncertainty_note: Exact non-compliance subtree id is uncertain; node selected as a broad placeholder.

title: Exposure of a child's academic record to the wrong parent or guardian
description: If the portal displays grades, teacher feedback, and submission history without strong verification of the parent's entitlement, a non-authorized parent, former guardian, or other user could view the child's educational records.
assumptions: The portal relies on an account-to-student relationship and may not always re-check guardianship or custody status before disclosure.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for unauthorized disclosure due to access-control failure; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may vary.

title: Linkability of multiple school activities through consolidated portal history
description: Displaying grades, feedback, and submission history together allows the parent to link separate assignments, teacher comments, and performance patterns over time into a detailed profile of the child.
assumptions: The flow presents multiple records in one view or account session.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit guess for linkability from aggregation in one interface.

title: Over-disclosure of detailed educational data beyond what is necessary
description: The portal may disclose more personal information than needed for the parent's purpose, such as full submission contents, extensive historical feedback, or sensitive comments, increasing privacy impact.
assumptions: Some displayed fields may not be strictly necessary for every parent interaction.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for excessive disclosure/data minimization issue; exact subnode uncertain.

title: Parent can plausibly deny having accessed sensitive student information
description: If access to grades and feedback is not reliably logged and attributable, the parent may later deny having viewed particular records, weakening accountability for access to the child's educational data.
assumptions: Audit logging, session binding, or access evidence may be incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit repudiation node; exact LINDDUN Pro numbering may differ.

title: Insufficient transparency to the child about parental access to school records
description: The child may be unaware that the portal reveals grades, feedback, and submission history to the parent, or may not know which items are shared and when they are viewed.
assumptions: The system does not provide clear notice to the child about disclosures to parents.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit detectability/unawareness-style node for lack of awareness; exact node id uncertain.

title: Disclosure to parent may conflict with consent, age, or educational privacy obligations
description: Showing detailed academic records to a parent could violate applicable policies or laws if the student has reached an age of independent rights, if consent/preferences are not respected, or if custody restrictions apply.
assumptions: Compliance obligations may vary by jurisdiction, student age, and guardianship arrangements.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node; exact subnode depends on the governing legal basis.

title: Administrative account-management actions can be linked to specific families or students
description: When the portal processes administrator changes to parent-child links and account records, those actions may be linkable to identifiable families, revealing that particular children are associated with specific parents/guardians and administrative interventions over time.
assumptions: The application stores audit trails, transaction logs, or change history containing identifiers for administrators, parents, and students.
uncertainty_note: Tree node selected as a best-fit generic linkability node; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ.

title: Parent-child relationships and account attributes may be identifiable from submitted data
description: The flow includes names, emails, roles, and parent-child relationships. If exposed through logs, debugging, browser history, admin dashboards, or intermediary components, the data can directly identify parents, children, and their associations.
assumptions: Personally identifiable data is present in requests or stored by the application and may be visible beyond the minimum necessary scope.
uncertainty_note: Node id is best-effort for identifiability via directly identifying attributes.

title: Administrator may be able to deny creating, modifying, or disabling accounts or links
description: If the portal does not create tamper-resistant, attributable records for account and relationship-management actions, an administrator could later repudiate having created, changed, or disabled an account or parent-child link.
assumptions: The flow results in state-changing operations and non-repudiation controls such as signed or integrity-protected audit logs may be absent or weak.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit generic non-repudiation node; exact subnode may vary by threat-tree version.

title: Administrative changes may disclose existence and status of accounts or relationships
description: Responses, error messages, or UI behavior during account creation, modification, or disabling can reveal whether a parent, child, or relationship already exists, has been disabled, or is associated with a particular school record.
assumptions: The portal returns distinguishable responses for existing vs non-existing accounts or valid vs invalid parent-child links.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit generic detectability/disclosure-related node; exact node id may differ.

title: Excessive collection or retention of names, emails, roles, and family links
description: The portal may collect or retain more account-management data than necessary for administration, such as preserving historical parent-child link changes indefinitely or storing unnecessary role/context attributes, enabling broader privacy impact over time.
assumptions: Business process or implementation may not enforce data minimization or retention limits for administrative updates.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for data minimization/retention concerns; exact subnode may differ.

title: Parents or students may be unaware of account and relationship changes affecting them
description: When an administrator creates, changes, or disables accounts and parent-child links, affected individuals may not be informed, making the processing insufficiently transparent and hindering their ability to verify correctness or challenge mistakes.
assumptions: The system does not notify affected parents/guardians or provide visibility into relationship and account status changes.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit generic unawareness node; exact subnode may vary.

title: Account and family-relationship management may violate purpose limitation or legal basis expectations
description: Managing names, emails, roles, and parent-child relationships without clear purpose limitation, authorization boundaries, retention rules, or appropriate notices/consent where required can create non-compliance with education and privacy obligations.
assumptions: Applicable policy or legal requirements constrain how school family relationship data may be created, changed, and retained.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit generic non-compliance node; exact node id depends on the specific LINDDUN Pro tree version and applicable jurisdiction.

title: Linkability of student and parent accounts via stored relationship links
description: Writing explicit parent-child relationship links into the account directory can enable linking multiple accounts belonging to the same family or household. If directory records are accessible across services or administrative domains, observers may correlate identities and activities across related accounts.
assumptions: The account directory stores explicit relationship identifiers or references that can be queried or inferred by internal services or administrators.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may vary depending on whether the relationship link is modeled as direct identifier linkage or association through metadata.

title: Identifiability of minors and guardians from account records
description: Account records written by the grading service may contain direct identifiers and relationship context that make both students and parents readily identifiable in the directory. The combination of names, account identifiers, and family-role information increases the ability to identify data subjects.
assumptions: Directory entries include direct or persistent identifiers and role labels such as student, parent, or guardian.
uncertainty_note: Node id chosen as a generic identifiability-from-direct-identifiers case; exact subnode may differ in a specific LINDDUN Pro catalog.

title: Disclosure of sensitive family relationship information
description: The write operation stores parent-child links in the account directory, revealing family relationships and potentially educational associations. Unauthorized access or overbroad internal access to the directory could expose sensitive information about a student's guardianship or household structure.
assumptions: The directory is accessible to multiple components, support staff, or administrators beyond the grading service.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for information disclosure due to directory storage; exact node may depend on the threat tree variant used.

title: Disclosure due to aggregation of account and grading-context data
description: Because the grading service is the source of the update, account directory records may implicitly reveal that a person participates in a grading or educational context. Aggregating account identity data with parent-child links can disclose more context than necessary to parties querying the directory.
assumptions: Consumers of the account directory can infer educational participation or role from records written by the grading service.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; this is an inference/aggregation-driven disclosure scenario and exact placement in LINDDUN Pro may differ.

title: Unawareness of creation and persistence of parent-child relationship records
description: Students and parents may be unaware that the grading service writes and persists family relationship links in the account directory, including who can access them and for what downstream purposes. Lack of visibility into this data flow undermines informed expectations about processing.
assumptions: The system does not clearly notify users that grading-related account maintenance includes storing guardian linkage in a shared directory.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for insufficient user awareness/transparency.

title: Excessive or incompatible storage of relationship data in directory
description: Writing parent-child links into a general account directory may exceed what is necessary for account administration or may be incompatible with the original purpose for which account data was collected. This can create non-compliance risk around purpose limitation, data minimization, and retention.
assumptions: The account directory is a general-purpose store and the relationship data is not strictly necessary for every directory use case.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; mapped as a generic non-compliance with purpose limitation/data minimization obligation.

title: Excessive disclosure of student and staff data in full backup replication
description: The nightly transfer sends full grade records, assignments, and the account directory to the cloud hosting provider. Replicating the entire dataset to a third party may disclose more personal data than is necessary for backup/hosting purposes, increasing exposure of sensitive academic and identity data.
assumptions: The provider receives or can technically access backup contents in identifiable form rather than only opaque, client-side encrypted blobs.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; I am confident about the disclosure threat, but the exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary by catalog version.

title: Provider-side access to backup contents reveals grades, assignments, and directory information
description: Once replicated to the external cloud hosting provider, provider administrators, support staff, or compromised provider systems could access the stored backups and hosting replicas, revealing sensitive educational records and account directory data.
assumptions: Backups or replicas are readable by the provider or by workloads under provider administrative control.
uncertainty_note: Threat clearly applies; node id is a best-effort mapping to provider/third-party disclosure.

title: Cross-system linkability of student activity and identity data
description: The combination of full grade records, assignments, and account directory information in one replicated dataset enables the cloud provider to link identifiers, coursework, performance history, and account attributes across systems and over time, creating rich linked profiles of individuals.
assumptions: The provider can observe or process multiple replicated data elements together and retain them across backup cycles.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; linkability is clear, but the precise LINDDUN Pro node numbering may differ.

title: Identifiability of students and staff from replicated backups
description: Because the backup includes the account directory alongside grades and assignments, individuals are directly identifiable within the replicated data, enabling the provider or an attacker at the provider to determine who a record belongs to.
assumptions: Account directory data includes direct identifiers such as names, usernames, email addresses, or institutional IDs.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability; numbering may differ across LINDDUN Pro versions.

title: Subjects may be unaware their educational records are replicated to a third-party host
description: Students and staff may not realize that their grades, assignments, and directory data are copied nightly to an external cloud hosting provider. This lack of visibility undermines users' awareness of where their personal data is stored and processed.
assumptions: Notices, dashboards, or policies do not clearly communicate this third-party backup/replication practice.
uncertainty_note: Threat applicability depends on transparency measures in place; node id is best-effort.

title: Third-party replication of educational records may exceed consent, contract, or regulatory expectations
description: Shipping full educational records and account directory data to an external provider may be incompatible with data-protection obligations or with the purposes originally communicated to students and staff, especially if full replicas are not strictly necessary or if cross-border storage is involved.
assumptions: There are legal, policy, or contractual limits on outsourcing, secondary processing, retention, or transfer of student records.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance depends strongly on jurisdiction, contracts, and notices; exact node id is a best-effort mapping.

title: Backups and replicas enable broad detectability of whether a person is in the system
description: The replicated account directory and academic records may allow the cloud provider or an attacker to detect whether a given individual is enrolled, has assignments, or has grade records, even without needing full contextual understanding of all contents.
assumptions: An adversary at or through the provider can query, inspect metadata, or otherwise determine presence of a person's records.
uncertainty_note: Detectability is plausible from directory and record presence; node id may not exactly match the target threat-tree edition.

title: Over-broad grade data disclosure in generated views
description: The grading service reads grade records to build views for students, parents, and teachers. If the service does not strictly filter records by viewer role and relationship, it may disclose one student's grades or feedback to unauthorized students, unrelated parents, or teachers without a legitimate educational relationship.
assumptions: P2 constructs multiple audience-specific views from the same underlying grade records and performs authorization/filtering before display.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id selected for disclosure from an application process; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may differ.

title: Secondary use of grade records across audience views
description: Grade records collected for assessment may be reused by the grading service to create broader student, parent, and teacher views than the data subject expects, potentially exposing detailed comments, historical performance, or metadata beyond the original grading purpose.
assumptions: The service may repurpose the same records for different stakeholder dashboards without granular purpose limitation.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit for unawareness/secondary use; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary.

title: Linkability of performance data across contexts
description: By aggregating grade records into different role-based views, the service can link a student's assessments across courses, time periods, and stakeholder interfaces, enabling broader profiling of academic performance than necessary for a single viewing context.
assumptions: P2 has access to identifiers and records spanning multiple assignments/classes and can correlate them when building views.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node chosen for linkability via aggregation/correlation in the service.

title: Identifiability of students from grade records
description: Even if some view elements are minimized, the grading service may render grade records together with direct identifiers or distinctive combinations of class, assignment, and score that make a student readily identifiable to viewers.
assumptions: Views include names or quasi-identifiers such as class, assignment title, timestamps, or teacher comments.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for identifiability from data presented by the process.

title: Insufficient evidence of access to grade records
description: If reads from the grade records database are not properly logged with requester identity, purpose, and scope, the school may be unable to prove which grade records were accessed to generate a given student, parent, or teacher view, hindering accountability and dispute resolution.
assumptions: DS2 or surrounding infrastructure may lack detailed, tamper-evident access logging for read operations.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-repudiation/accountability on read access; exact subtree may differ.

title: Processing of grade data beyond policy or consent constraints
description: The grading service may read and present grade records to parents, students, and teachers in ways that conflict with educational privacy policies, local regulations, age-based consent rules, or role-specific access restrictions.
assumptions: Applicable policy constraints may differ by student age, custody/guardian status, staff role, or institution rules.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance due to unauthorized or over-broad processing.
